title: helm(private): stabilize values schema + init hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Improve and stabilize the Helm chart for redwood-private by hardening values schema, making init hook behavior deterministic during upgrades, and adding explicit rollback-safe steps. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in regulated environments reported intermittent failures during chart upgrades (lost secrets, init job races, and schema validation errors). This PR makes the chart tolerant to mixed-version upgrades and documents a recommended upgrade path.

What changed (high level):
- Add a versioned values schema (values.schema.json) with explicit allowed/required fields for encryption, KMS, tolerations, nodeSelector, and networkPolicy.
- Introduce an owner-ref aware init job (templates/init-secrets-job.yaml) that runs as a pre-upgrade hook and migrates legacy Kubernetes Secrets -> sealed secrets format used by installer; it retries idempotently and uses ConfigMap locks to avoid parallel runs.
- Add pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks with hook deletion policies to ensure deterministic cleanup on rollback.
- Improve templating for tolerations/nodeSelector so new keys don't remove existing user-specified values (preserve merge semantics).
- Add an annotation-driven feature-flag to enable/disable the init job for air-gapped installs.
- Add integration tests for upgrade and rollback scenarios (chart/tests/upgrade-rollback-test.yaml).

Checklist: 
- [x] values.schema.json added and referenced in Chart.yaml
- [x] init hook implemented with idempotency and locking
- [x] templating changes covered with unit tests (helm-unittest)
- [x] integration upgrade/rollback test added (CI)
- [x] migration instructions documented in CHART_UPGRADES.md

Commits (summary):
- feat(helm): add values.schema.json and map required fields (Asha)
- fix(helm): make tolerations merge instead of replace (Samir)
- feat(helm): add pre-upgrade init-secrets-job hook with ConfigMap lock (Asha)
- docs(charts): CHART_UPGRADES.md with upgrade steps and rollback notes (Elena)
- test(helm): add upgrade-rollback integration test and CI job (Miguel)

Files changed (high level):
- charts/redwood-private/values.schema.json (new)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/init-secrets-job.yaml (new, pre-upgrade hook)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/hooks/_helpers.tpl (updated)
- charts/redwood-private/templates/deployment.yaml (tolerations/nodeSelector merge)
- charts/redwood-private/CHART_UPGRADES.md (new)
- charts/redwood-private/tests/upgrade-rollback-test.yaml (new)
- .github/workflows/helm-integration.yml (CI job updated)
- charts/redwood-private/Chart.yaml (chart version bump)

Testing and CI: The new helm integration job runs the upgrade -> post-upgrade -> rollback matrix using kind clusters and validated the following matrix on CI:
- upgrade from chart v1.8.x -> v1.9.0 with legacy secrets present
- rollback from v1.9.0 -> v1.8.x successfully cleans hooks and reverts in cluster
CI initially failed on first run due to chart lint rule for schema refs; fixed by committing explicit $schema and examples. Final CI status: pass.

Migration notes: Users on older Private installs should follow CHART_UPGRADES.md which recommends running the init hook once before full cluster upgrade when running in multi-control-plane clusters. The hook can be disabled with annotation 'redwood.io/init-hook: "disabled"' for air-gapped installs. Backwards compatibility: values.schema.json is versioned; chart supports both legacy and new keys for one release cycle and logs warnings when legacy keys are used.

Release notes: Stabilize private Helm chart upgrade/rollback behavior; add safer init job for secrets migration; schema validation for values to catch misconfigs during CI.
commits: 5 commits: feat(helm): add values.schema.json; fix(helm): tolerations merge semantics; feat(helm): pre-upgrade init-secrets-job; docs: CHART_UPGRADES.md; test(helm): add upgrade-rollback integration test
review_thread:
Miguel Rivera: Can the init job be made optional for air-gapped installs?
Asha Patel: yes, added annotation flag 'redwood.io/init-hook: "disabled"' and documented in CHART_UPGRADES.md.
Elena Zhou: The schema change might break some customers, add migration text.
Asha Patel: Added migration section and retained legacy keys for one release cycle; CI emits deprecation warnings.
Samir Kothari: Why are we using a ConfigMap lock instead of leader-election?
Asha Patel: ConfigMap lock keeps the hook simple (no controller) and works across Helm upgrades and jobs; documented failure modes.
Miguel Rivera: Approving after CI passes.
Elena Zhou: Approved.
Merge: squash
release_notes: Stabilize Helm chart for Redwood Private: add values schema validation, idempotent init hook for secret migration, improved templating for tolerations/nodeSelector, and upgrade/rollback integration tests.
migration_instructions: See charts/redwood-private/CHART_UPGRADES.md for step-by-step instructions. Recommended: run the init hook with helm upgrade --install --set redwood.io/init-hook.enabled=true before upgrading control planes in multi-cluster setups. To disable for air-gapped installs set redwood.io/init-hook: "disabled" in values.yaml.
test_plan: Unit tests (helm-unittest) for templating changes + integration CI that runs upgrade->verify->rollback matrix on kind clusters. Manual: validated on customer-like staging cluster with legacy secrets.
